q: What will a lender want to see for a compressed air upgrade loan?
title: Compressed air upgrade loan: what to show
short: Show 6 to 12 months of electricity bills and compressor run hours before the upgrade, the supplier quote with rated specific power, and a leak survey. After installation, show the same records again. The saving in kWh times the grid factor is the carbon benefit lenders can read.
audience: Factories replacing old compressors or fixing leaks with a loan

ul: Compressor run and load hours, or a sub-meter reading.
Leak survey or air audit report.
Same bills and run hours for the same months.
Commissioning report for the new compressor or dryer.

p: A measured baseline, a clear link between the asset and the saving, and figures that compare like with like after allowing for production changes.

example.title: Worked example
lines: Before: 18,000 kWh a month on compressors
After: 13,500 kWh a month for the same output
Saving: 4,500 kWh x 0.710 kg (FY 2024-25) = 3.2 t CO2 a month, about 38 t a year
example.note: Illustrative. Use your own sub-meter or bill figures.

senseible: Senseible measures your baseline from your own bills before the project and keeps measuring after it, so the saving you show a lender comes from documents, not a brochure. Lenders decide on the loan.
